kfn.description: Exact k farthest-neighbor search (k=10) over road-network object sets (real POI categories and uniform densities up to d=0.1; on train and test also regional object sets and map-spread query vertices). Benefit: how few objects a method has to retrieve individually and how few exact network distances it computes, relative to evaluating every object. Constraints: every answer exact, index size and index construction work within budget.
kfn.notes: colt / colt_default / alt_filter / bruteforce rows: this workspace's reference runs on the public train split (scripts/evaluate_train.sh -> scoring/scores_train.json; the same workload families as the hidden test: real POI categories and uniform d = 0.001, 0.01, 0.1 from vertex-uniform and map-spread sources, plus regional object sets for kFN), job fe5c0106-435. The _paper_setting_* rows are the same methods in the paper's own setting (scripts/evaluate.sh -> eval/evaluate.py -> scoring/scores.json: original NW travel times, the eight real POI categories as published plus uniform d = 0.001, 0.01, 0.1, public query seed). The hidden-test rows are in scoring/scores_test.json. colt uses the paper's Table 8 kFN structure (b=4, m=4, Slice landmarks, 16 random ALT root landmarks) with two index parameters set by the paper's own procedure (parameter testing, Section 9.6) on this network's public train split, one at a time: lambda=16 (method/tuned_lambda.json; the paper's 256 was tuned on its 22x larger network), then the random draw of the 16 ALT landmarks, best of six draws (seed 6, method/tuned_root.json; single draws differ consistently by ~0.1 log10 candidates on this network). alt_filter (the paper's AUB-PHL) uses the same ALT draw, as in the paper. colt_default uses the paper's untuned defaults (b=8, m=2, Random, lambda=256, default draw seed 1). Candidates count individually retrieved objects plus opened non-empty index nodes (the paper counts objects only); calls count every exact distance, including those to landmarks (the paper counts distances to objects only). Scale: the NW subset (1.09M vertices) of the paper's 24M-vertex US network, Dijkstra instead of PHL, so the paper's numbers are kept under _paper_* keys: read off the paper's log-scale Figure 11c/11d (continental US, uniform objects at d=0.0001, ~2.4k objects), approximate.

log10_candidate_reduction.description: Mean over queries of log10((|P|+1)/(candidates+1)), floored at 0. Candidates = objects revealed individually + non-empty index nodes accessed; 0 = every object retrieved individually.

log10_call_reduction.description: Mean over queries of log10((|Q||P|+1)/(exact distance computations+1)); 0 = brute force.

exact_answer_rate.description: Fraction of exact answers (ties at the k-th distance accepted). Any wrong answer, crash or protocol violation scores the method with the worst value of every metric.

index_entries_per_vertex.description: Landmark distance-list entries per road-network vertex (index size). Capped at 40 for kFN.

sdl_work_per_vertex.description: Vertices settled while building the landmark distance lists, per vertex (index construction cost). Capped at 3000 for kfn.

aknn.description: Exact aggregate k nearest-neighbor search (k=10, |Q|=8 query vertices drawn from a 15% subnetwork, max and sum aggregates). Same benefit and constraint metrics as kfn. On train and test, half of the query areas are centred spread over the map (5% of the vertices).
aknn.notes: Same provenance as kfn (job fe5c0106-435): method rows from the public train split, _paper_setting_* rows from the paper's own setting. colt uses the paper's Table 8 AkNN structure (b=8, m=2, Random) with lambda=32 and the ALT root-landmark draw (seed 2, best of six) both tested on the train split; alt_filter uses the same ALT draw; colt_default uses lambda=256 and the default draw. _paper_colt_phl is read off the paper's Figure 8b (max aggregate, A=15%, d=0.001, ~24k objects on the 24M-vertex network) and is approximate.

range.description: Exact range search (radius 2.5% of the network diameter). Same benefit and constraint metrics as kfn.
range.notes: Same provenance as kfn (job fe5c0106-435): method rows from the public train split, _paper_setting_* rows from the paper's own setting. colt uses the paper's Table 8 range structure (b=8, m=2, Border Minmax) with lambda=32 and the ALT root-landmark draw (seed 2, best of six) both tested on the train split; alt_filter uses the same ALT draw; colt_default uses b=8, m=2, Random, lambda=256 and the default draw. _paper_colt_phl is read off the paper's Figure 13d (r=2.5% D, d=0.0001, ~2.4k objects) and is approximate.
